title: G01. Two similarities sharing a secant
statement: In an acute triangle $ABC$ with orthocenter $H$, complete the parallelogram $ABGH$. On line $GH$ choose $I$ so that $AC$ passes through the midpoint of $HI$. Let $J\ne C$ be the other intersection of $AC$ with $(GCI)$. Prove $IJ=AH$.

title: G02. Reflect the two lines
statement: Triangle $ABC$ lies on a circle $\Omega$ with center $O$. A circle centered at $A$ cuts $BC$ at $D,E$ in the order $B,D,E,C$, and cuts the arcs $AB$ and $AC$ of $\Omega$ not containing the third vertex at $F,G$, respectively. Let $K\ne B$ be the intersection of $AB$ with $(BDF)$, and $L\ne C$ the intersection of $AC$ with $(CEG)$. If distinct lines $FK,GL$ meet at $X$, prove $A,X,O$ collinear.

title: G03. An angle condition is a distance locus
statement: Let $I$ be the incenter of $ABC$. An interior point $P$ satisfies $\angle PBA+\angle PCA=\angle PBC+\angle PCB$. Prove $AP\ge AI$, with equality only at $P=I$.

title: G04. Reflection completes a cyclicity proof
statement: In cyclic quadrilateral $ABCD$, the diagonals meet at $E$. The extensions of $AD,BC$ beyond $A,B$ meet at $F$. Complete parallelogram $ECGD$, and reflect $E$ in $AD$ to obtain $H$. Prove $D,H,F,G$ concyclic.

title: G05. Reflected lines meet on the mirror
statement: Let $M,N$ be the midpoints of $AB,AC$, and $T$ the midpoint of the arc $BC$ not containing $A$ on $(ABC)$. The circle $(AMT)$ meets the perpendicular bisector of $AC$ at an interior point $X$ of $ABC$; similarly $(ANT)$ meets the perpendicular bisector of $AB$ at an interior point $Y$. If $K=MN\cap XY$, prove $KA=KT$.

title: G06. Double the cevians
statement: In an acute triangle, choose $P,Q$ on $BC$ with $\angle PAB=C$ and $\angle QAC=B$. Extend $AP,AQ$ to $M,N$ so that $PM=PA$ and $QN=QA$. Show that $BM$ and $CN$ meet on $(ABC)$.

title: G07. Pack two similar triangles
statement: Points $K,L,M$ on $BC,CA,AB$ have concurrent cevians $AK,BL,CM$. Prove that two of $ALM,BMK,CKL$ have inradii whose sum is at least the inradius $r$ of $ABC$.

title: G08. Convert intersection ratios into half angles
statement: Let $I$ be the incenter, $M$ the midpoint of $BC$, and $D$ the foot from $I$ to $BC$. The perpendicular to $AI$ through $I$ meets $AB,AC$ at $F,E$. Let $X\ne A$ be the other common point of $(AEF)$ and $(ABC)$. Prove that $XD$ and $AM$ meet on $(ABC)$.

title: G09. The hidden orthocenter of a pentagon
statement: A convex pentagon $ABCDE$ satisfies $AB=BC=CD$, $\angle EAB=\angle BCD$, and $\angle EDC=\angle CBA$. Prove that $AC,BD$ and the perpendicular from $E$ to $BC$ concur.

title: G10. A half-turn creates the tangent
statement: Points $R,S$ lie on $\Omega$, and $R'=2S-R$. Let $I$ lie on the smaller arc $RS$. The circle $\Gamma=(ISR')$ meets the tangent to $\Omega$ at $R$ twice; call the nearer intersection to $R$ point $A$. If $AI$ meets $\Omega$ again at $J$, prove $JR'$ tangent to $\Gamma$.

title: G11. Two tangents encode a reflection
statement: A circle through $A$ meets $AB,AC$ again at $D,E$ and crosses $BC$ at $F,G$ in that order. Tangents at $F$ to $(BDF)$ and at $G$ to $(CEG)$ meet at $T\ne A$. Prove $AT\parallel BC$.

title: G12. Close two circles around the target point
statement: In parallelogram $ABCD$, assume $AC=BC$. Take $P$ beyond $B$ on $AB$. Let $Q\ne D$ be the intersection of $PD$ with $(ACD)$, and $R\ne P$ the intersection of $PC$ with $(APQ)$. Prove $CD,AQ,BR$ concurrent.

title: G13. A circle equation linearizes the ratio
statement: In an acute triangle $ABC$, let $M$ be the midpoint of $AC$. A circle through $B,M$ meets $BA,BC$ again at $P,Q$. Complete parallelogram $BPTQ$, and assume $T\in(ABC)$. Determine $BT/BM$.

title: G14. Transfer a tangent through equal powers
statement: An acute triangle $ABC$ has $AB>AC$, orthocenter $H$, base midpoint $M$, and altitude foot $F$ on $BC$. On its circumcircle $\Omega$, choose $Q,K$ so that $\angle AQH=\angle QKH=90^\circ$. Prove that $(KQH)$ and $(KFM)$ are tangent at $K$.

title: G15. Equal segments turn spiral similarity into rotation
statement: A cyclic quadrilateral satisfies $AC<BD<AD$ and $\angle DBA<90^\circ$. On the side of $AD$ opposite $C$, choose $E$ with $DE\parallel AB$, $DE=AC$, and $F$ with $AF\parallel CD$, $AF=BD$. Prove that the perpendicular bisectors of $BC,EF$ meet on $(ABCD)$.

title: G16. Reflect a vertex in the incenter
statement: A triangle has $AB<AC<BC$, incenter $I$, and incircle. The other tangent parallel to $AC$ meets the interior of $BC$ at $X$; the other tangent parallel to $AB$ meets it at $Y$. Let $P\ne A$ be the intersection of $AI$ with $(ABC)$, and let $K,L$ be the midpoints of $AB,AC$. Prove $\angle KIL+\angle YPX=180^\circ$.
